key_insight: The EHR-integrated GenAI tool identified inpatient VTE risk more sensitively than either checklist-based or clinician-judgment order sets, though specificity was lower than the checklist approach.
clinical_relevance: For hospitals, this suggests GenAI may help catch more patients who need thromboprophylaxis support, but it should be implemented with attention to false positives and workflow fit.
method: Retrospective multisite validation at Johns Hopkins Medicine
Random sample of 500 adult inpatient admissions from 758 eligible cases
Compared iHGR and clinician-selected order sets against physician-adjudicated chart review as the reference standard
evidence_signal: In this validation dataset, iHGR reached 81.8% sensitivity and 70.9% specificity, outperforming the checklist order set on sensitivity and the clinician-judgment order set on sensitivity with comparable specificity trade-offs.
watch_item: False negatives were linked to missed narrative risk factors, highlighting the challenge of extracting nuanced clinical context from EHR text and the need for careful human oversight.
paper_title: Multisite Real-World Validation of an Electronic Health Record-Integrated Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool for Venous Thromboembolism Risk Stratification
